questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,11,1)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨2,-5,4⟩=20.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,-5,4⟩ & =20 \\ 2x-5y+4z & =20 \\ 4z & =20-2x+5y \\ z & =5-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{4}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=2$ and $y=4,$ we get 

$$
z=5-\frac{1}{2}(2)+\frac{5}{4}(4)=9.
$$

So, the point $Q(2,4,9)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,4,9⟩-⟨-2,11,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-7,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨2,-5,4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(4)\cdot 2+(-7)\cdot (-5)+8\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|8+35+32|}{\sqrt{4+25+16}} \\  & =\frac{|75|}{\sqrt{45}} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-11,-8,-4)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $14x+8y-8z=-6.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=-2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}14x+8y-8z & =-6 \\ 14(-1)+8(-2)-8z & =-6 \\ -8z & =24 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,-2,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,-2,-3⟩-⟨-11,-8,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨10,6,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨14,8,-8⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|10\cdot 14+6\cdot 8+1\cdot (-8)|}{\sqrt{(14)^{2}+{8}^{2}+(-8)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|140+48-8|}{\sqrt{196+64+64}} \\  & =\frac{|\,180\,|}{\sqrt{324}} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,11,10)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-2x-4y+4z=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=2$ and $y=3$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-4y+4z & =16 \\ -2(2)-4(3)+4z & =16 \\ 4z & =32 \\ z & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,3,8)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,8⟩-⟨-1,11,10⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-8,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-2,-4,4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot (-2)+(-8)\cdot (-4)+(-2)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6+32-8|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,18\,|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $Q(5,-1,9)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨3,-6,-2⟩=3$, find the shortest distance from $P(7,-2,8)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨5,-1,9⟩-⟨7,-2,8⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨3,-6,-2⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-2)\cdot 3+1\cdot (-6)+1\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6-6-2|}{\sqrt{9+36+4}} \\  & =\frac{|-14|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{14}{7} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,4,-5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-2x+2y+z=6.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+2y+z & =6 \\ -2(1)+2(1)+z & =6 \\ z & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,1,6)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,1,6⟩-⟨-1,4,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-3,11⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-2,2,1⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot 2+11\cdot 1|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4-6+11|}{\sqrt{4+4+1}} \\  & =\frac{|1|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
